episodes.204381: A cold front swept through southern New England in the afternoon bringing a line of storms, a few of which were severe. These caused sporadic wind damage and some limited flash flooding in northeast MA.
episodes.204383: A stalled front draped from SW to NE across southern New England helped to initiate a severe thunderstorm over the south shore of MA. This storm caused sporadic wind damage and produced 1.5 inch hail.
episodes.204454: Most gusty outflow winds were throughout northern Utah.
episodes.204683: Stationary thunderstorms along the Bay Breeze resulted in localized rainfall amounts of two to four inches near Baltimore in an hour or two.
episodes.204740: A couple of thunderstorms produced localized gale-force wind gusts over the tidal Patapsco River and the middle tidal Potomac River.
episodes.204818: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along a prefrontal trough across the Coastal Plain of Eastern North Carolina during the morning of August fourteenth. Showers and thunderstorms then tracked east, merging into linear segments during the afternoon. A few isolated thunderstorms became strong to severe in nature. This brought strong and damaging wind gusts to the inland sounds and rivers across Eastern North Carolina.
episodes.204912: Scattered showers and thunderstorms blossomed across the area on the 13th of August as a cold front slowly approached from the northwest. The front eventually reached the Ohio River around midnight and then proceeded southeast through West Virginia by the afternoon of the 14th. In addition to producing heavy downpours, thunderstorms began training across portions of southeast Ohio and southwest West Virginia. These heavy showers and storms generally produced two to five inches of rain in southeastern Lawrence County, though one rain gage near Proctorville registered a rainfall amount of almost seven inches. This excessive rainfall caused flooding of roads in the towns of Rome and Proctorville. Flooding came to an end as precipitation shifted south and then tapered off before daybreak on the 14th.
episodes.204914: Scattered showers and thunderstorms blossomed across the area on the 13th of August as a cold front slowly approached from the northwest. The front eventually reached the Ohio River around midnight and then proceeded southeast through West Virginia by the afternoon of the 14th. ||In addition to producing heavy downpours, thunderstorms began training across portions of southeast Ohio and southwest West Virginia during this timeframe. These heavy showers and storms produced one to two inches of rain across much of northeastern West Virginia, with pockets of two to four inches prompting some flash flooding in Wood, Wirt, and Roane Counties during the afternoon and evening. Down towards the I-64 corridor, training storms produced a swath of two to five inch rainfall amounts across portions of Cabell County, which resulted in street flooding in Huntington during the night. Flooding came to an end as precipitation shifted south and then tapered off before daybreak on the 14th.
episodes.205364: Scattered thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall during the evening hours.
episodes.205502: Gusty winds from a decaying shower brought strong winds to a narrow corridor north of Boulder, where the peak gust measured 72 mph. Stronger storms (mainly sub-severe) developed over the plains with up to one inch hail over eastern Elbert County.
episodes.205816: A weak upper level disturbance extended across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northwest Louisiana on August 14th, in an area where afternoon temperatures climbed to near and in excess of 100 degrees. Given the moist and very unstable air mass in place, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon across portions of the Four State Region, with one isolated severe thunderstorm producing damaging winds which downed a tree northeast of the Jamestown community in Bienville Parish.
episodes.205894: Moist and unsettled southwest steering flow triggered afternoon and evening showers and storms over an unstable airmass. A few strong to pulse severe storms formed along boundary mergers.
episodes.205895: Moist and unsettled southwest steering flow triggered afternoon and evening showers and storms over an unstable airmass. A few strong to pulse severe storms formed along boundary mergers.
episodes.206487: Received reports of severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.206513: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the northern Nebraska Panhandle and southwestern South Dakota during the early evening hours of August 13th. This activity became better organized as a bow echo as it tracked east across far northern Nebraska into the evening hours. This activity eventually exited Wheeler and Holt counties after 2 AM CDT on August 14th. Hail up to golf ball size and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 65 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.206595: Slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.206612: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a prefrontal trough and again along lake and residual outflow boundaries. With PWAT values near 2.00 inches, some storms did produce efficient rainfall for flash flooding.
episodes.206627: Hot and humid conditions created a cumulus field and supported convective initiation. A pulse storm developed in southeastern Shelby County and produced localized tree damage and small hail.
episodes.206628: An isolated cell developed in southwestern Lac Qui Parle County around 3pm and quickly strengthened and moved into the northeastern portion of the county. The storm produced large hail up to 1.25 inches just northeast of Dawson before dissipating as it crossed the Chippewa county line.
episodes.206659: An upper level disturbance slowly moved across Louisiana allowing for scattered showers and storms to develop during the afternoons of mid-August. The slow motion and high rain rate produced flooding in Alexandria.
episodes.206671: Scattered showers and storms developed in Western Kentucky during the afternoon hours of the 14th. A torrential downpour produced street flooding in Hopkinsville while numerous photos were taken of the funnel cloud in eastern Daviess County late afternoon.
episodes.206701: Thunderstorms developed in the warm humid airmass across portions of east-central and Downeast Maine during the afternoon of the 14th in advance of a cold front. Isolated storms reached severe levels producing damaging winds.
episodes.206751: Two clusters of storms would move across the forecast area on the 13th into the early morning hours of the 14th. The day started with an isolated stronger storm generating 1 inch hail 6 miles north northeast of Lowry. That cluster would continue to move east and intensify, with 1.5 inch hail observed 8 miles east of Pierpont. These storms would damage siding and crops around Pierpont, with additional thunderstorm wind damage to trees in the town of Roslyn. ||Another cluster of storms would move through central South Dakota, with a peak wind gust of 73 mph recorded by the South Dakota State University mesonet station 12 miles south of Vivian. As this cluster departed and weakened, additional winds were generated, with a gust of 68 mph 3 miles southeast of Reliance on a South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station.||A total of 3.6 inches was observed 6 miles east southeast of Pierpont. This rainfall, on top of already saturated soils from the previous month's heavy rains, resulted in water over roads, a partial washout, and at least one stranded vehicle in this area. In Roslyn, a trained spotter recorded 4.64 inches.
episodes.206826: Thunderstorms initiated along the higher terrain of western South Dakota and moved eastward through a stout instability axis from 2000-2500 J/kg MUCAPE and deep-layer shear up to 40 knots. However, the storms quickly outran the better parameters and weakened moving into southeast South Dakota, but not before linear storms produced areas of 60 to 65 mph wind across Gregory County. Additional storms developed several hours later during the early morning hours with isolated wind damage southeast of Huron.
episodes.206827: An isolated elevated supercell developed across west central Minnesota within an area of scattered thunderstorms during the mid to late afternoon hours and dropped slowly southward through early evening. The storm dropped large hail moving southward into Lyon County before weakening.
episodes.207063: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in an atmosphere rich with high moisture values. This moisture was realized as locally heavy rainfall. One thunderstorm in Rockbridge County had enough heavy rain in a concentrated area to bring damaging wind gusts to the surface, downing around thirty trees near Rockbridge Baths.
episodes.207092: A late-summer hot and humid airmass was in place across most of Virginia on August 14. Additionally, a slow-moving cold front stalled over central and southeast Virginia in the afternoon, supporting thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding in southeast Virginia during the evening hours.
episodes.207104: Mid-level atmospheric moisture moved over Wyoming causing scattered high-based showers and thunderstorms to develop. With dew point depressions greater than 50 degrees, wind gusts of 50 knots or higher were reported in portions of Johnson, Natrona, Sublette, and Sweetwater Counties.
episodes.207105: Monsoonal moisture fueled high-based thunderstorms and strong outflow wind gusts. The highest gust reported was 80 mph in Red Canyon near South Pass. Wind gusts over 60 mph were also reported in Washakie and Park Counties.
episodes.207130: A late-summer hot and humid airmass was in place across the lower Maryland Eastern Shore on August 14. Additionally, a slow-moving cold front stalled southern Maryland, extending southwest in Virginia. Showers and storms with heavy rainfall produced localized flooding in the Salisbury area in the afternoon.
episodes.207163: A hot and unstable airmass was firmly in place across the Seacoast on the afternoon of August 14th.  A weak frontal boundary triggered a few isolated thunderstorms, with one of the storms becoming severe across coastal Rockingham County.
episodes.207184: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi during the afternoon and evening hours of August 13th through 17th. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with the strongest of storms.
episodes.207185: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northeast Louisiana during the afternoon hours of August 14th. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with the strongest of storms, and a few land spout type funnel clouds were observed.
episodes.207193: A squall line developed during and brought severe wind gusts across western SD.
episodes.207689: A slow moving cold front moved west to east across northern Ohio during the afternoon and evening hours of August 13th, 2025. A warm and moist environment, characterized by MLCAPE values between 1500-2000 j/kg and precipitable water values near 1.8 inches, and weak deep layer shear promoted slow moving thunderstorms producing efficient rainfall. An area of slow moving and training thunderstorms produced excessive rainfall and isolated flash flooding in the Youngstown area during the early evening hours.
